In the Kumārasambhava

"May you obtain the unbroken love of your husband," the virtuous women said to her, and Umā bowed in response. But she, having become half the body of him <note>Lord Shiva</note>, made even the blessings of her affectionate kin seem trivial. 28

Commentary: "Unbroken"—meaning unimpaired—was the love of her husband, Shiva, which she was told to obtain. The use of the present tense with the particle "sma" denotes the past. By becoming half of his body, Gauri rendered the blessings of her relatives secondary; the implication is that she had attained a result far greater than any mere blessing could provide.

Having completed the duties appropriate to his desire and his resources, the mountain <note>Himālaya</note>, capable and acting with decorum in the assembly, stood waiting for the arrival of the Lord marked by the bull <note>Shiva</note> in the hall occupied by his friends. 29

Commentary: The mountain, Himālaya, was capable and knew the protocols of the assembly. He ensured that everything done for Pārvatī was in accordance with his own ambitions and his wealth, leaving no task unfinished. He waited in the hall, which was filled with guests, for the arrival of Shiva.

At that very moment, upon the mountain of Kubera <note>Kailāsa</note>, the Mothers <note>the seven divine mother-goddesses</note>, who had been summoned, placed before the Destroyer of the City <note>Shiva</note> the ornaments appropriate for his previous hand-taking <note>his marriage to Pārvatī</note>. 30

Commentary: Just as Pārvatī’s preparations were being completed, the seven Mother-goddesses arrived on Mount Kailāsa. They presented to Shiva the traditional ornaments required for the wedding rites.

<summary>This page describes Pārvatī receiving blessings from virtuous women, Himālaya’s preparations for the arrival of Shiva, and the seven Mother-goddesses bringing wedding ornaments to Shiva.</summary>
